arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case's counsel argued that Section 2255(h) incorporates the certification process for second or successive applications.
the side that brought the case's counsel stated that this incorporation prohibits review by petition for writ of certiorari.
The government's counsel argued that Congress passed AEDPA to advance the finality of criminal convictions.
The government's counsel noted that Congress largely eliminated post-conviction applications by federal prisoners.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the scope of Supreme Court jurisdiction over federal prisoner habeas petitions. the side that brought the case argues the Court lacks power to review the case. The government argues the Court retains authority to decide the matter.

The government argues that Congress intended to preserve Supreme Court jurisdiction over these specific petitions.
